name: llmwise
description: Ask another AI model a question, or ask two or three at once and see their answers side by side, using your llmwise account.

interface.longDescription:
llmwise lets you ask the AI models in your llmwise account without leaving the conversation.

Ask one model a question when you want a second opinion, or name the model you want. Or ask two or three models the same question at once and see each answer under the model's name, side by side.

You can name the models yourself or let them be picked for you. Each answer comes straight from the model you picked. Questions count toward your llmwise account's messages, the same as messages you send on llmwise.ai, and aren't saved to your llmwise chats.

To connect, sign in with your llmwise email link and confirm the connection. You can disconnect at any time in your settings.
capabilities: List the AI models your llmwise account can use
Ask one model a question and get its answer
Ask two or three models the same question and compare their answers
defaultPrompt: Get a second opinion on this from another model
Compare two models on this question
Ask three models and show their answers side by side

positive.description: See which models the account can use.
positive.prompt: Which AI models can I use through llmwise?
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls list_models and lists the models the account can use, each with its maker and a one-line description (for example Claude Sonnet 5.5 by Anthropic, Gemini 3.1 Pro by Google, DeepSeek V4 Pro by DeepSeek).

positive.description: Ask one named model a question.
positive.prompt: Ask Claude Sonnet 5.5 on llmwise to explain the difference between TCP and UDP in three sentences.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls ask_model with model_id claude-sonnet-5-5 (calling list_models first if it needs the id) and shows Claude Sonnet 5.5's three-sentence answer, attributed to Claude Sonnet 5.5.

positive.description: Get a second opinion from another model.
positive.prompt: Get a second opinion from Gemini on llmwise: is it safe to store user passwords hashed with plain SHA-256?
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls ask_model with a Gemini model id (gemini-3.1-pro-preview) and shows Gemini's answer, which explains that a fast hash like SHA-256 isn't suitable on its own and recommends a slow, salted password hash such as Argon2, bcrypt or scrypt.

positive.description: Compare two models side by side.
positive.prompt: Use llmwise to compare GPT-6 Sol and DeepSeek V4 Pro: write a haiku about autumn rain.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT calls compare_models with model_ids gpt-6-sol and deepseek-v4-pro and shows two haikus, each under its model's name.

positive.description: Compare three models on a technical question.
positive.prompt: Ask three different models on llmwise which sorting algorithm works best on nearly sorted data, and show their answers side by side.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT picks three model ids (from list_models if needed), calls compare_models once with all three, and shows three answers under their models' names; each names an algorithm such as insertion sort or Timsort and says why.

negative.description: A general question that doesn't ask for another model: ChatGPT answers itself.
A writing task with no mention of llmwise or another model.
negative.prompt: Write a short poem about the sea.

negative.description: A request about something llmwise doesn't do.
negative.prompt: Book me a table for two at an Italian restaurant tonight.

publication.release_notes: First release: list_models, ask_model and compare_models, with answers shown side by side in ChatGPT.
